class: A guard against repeating an action also blocked the remedy the rules prescribe
symptom: Mutual of Enumclaw (iCIMS), 29 September, 18:54, the run after f064's fix: the owner solved the CAPTCHA, the agent gave the email, reached 'Enter Your Password' and stopped with 'sign-in on login.icims.com is paused to protect the account' -- without typing anything and without the reset. The owner asked how it knew the page was blocked without trying.
site: iCIMS (login.icims.com); any site whose refusal was recorded by an earlier run
root_cause: login_guard keeps a refusal across runs ('hold: rejected') so a refused password is not typed again. attempt_auto_login read that hold and stopped before typing, which is right, but the reset (f064) only followed a refusal seen in this run -- a WRONG_PASSWORD page or a rejection just produced -- so a refusal remembered from an earlier run reached no reset at all: the guard stood in for the refusal and swallowed its remedy.
why_tests_missed: f064's tests produced the refusal inside the test (a rejected attempt, or a page showing the message); none began a run with the refusal already on record, as every real resumed run does.
fix: login_guard.refused_before answers whether this account's last sign-in here was refused; account_state's table treats a sign-in page with that record like the refusal itself: RESET_PASSWORD for a known account not yet reset this run, otherwise the owner's -- never another try of the password. A reset that stops now says why on the dashboard (the site sent a link, no code step, no code in Gmail), and 'instructions to reset' is read as a link. Policy update, 12 October 2026 (f154): the owner removed persisted rejection holds. Historical reset behavior is retained here as incident context; persisted history is now diagnostic only, while current portal refusals still govern live recovery.
prevention: A remembered fact is the same fact: a decision table reads what earlier runs recorded as well as what the page shows now, and a fix for a situation is tested starting from each way a run can arrive at it -- fresh, and resumed with the record already written. Current regression references cover the owner-requested removal of cross-run holds and retain live rejection/reset coverage.
